newsitem.title: FRANCE: France to quit Central African Republic - paper.
newsitem.headline: France to quit Central African Republic - paper.

text.p: France has decided to close down its garrison in the Central African Republic as part of a new policy of reducing forces and commitments in Africa, Liberation newspaper said on Thursday.
The decision will be announced to President Ange-Felix Patasse by Defence Minister Alain Richard when he tours several African capitals next week, it added.
Richard's office confirmed the trip was taking place, without saying which capitals would be visited, but otherwise declined to comment.

Officials of France's new Socialist administration have publicly spoken of "reorganisation" of French troop presence in former African colonies as well as of "disengagement" but have not been specific.

Liberation said the troubled internal situation in the Central African Republic, where part of the army has mutinied and holds some areas of the capital Bangui, was one reason why France had decided to pull out.
Paris would close its bases in Bangui and in Bouar further north, reducing its troop presence from 1,400 to nil or perhaps maintaining a maximum 100 men at Bangui airport, the newspaper said.

The number of troops in the Red Sea port republic of Djibouti would drop to 2,800 from 3,250, the number in Chad would drop to 550 from 840 while troop strength in Senegal and Gabon, now at 1,300 and 600 respectively, would drop to 1,100 and 550.
The garrison in the Ivory Coast would remain unchanged at 550 men, the newspaper said.
